text: Monday's training day at the Harbour Street office went smoothly. Priya arrived first and picked the seat nearest the window. The morning session covered the new expense system, and most people found it easier than the old one. Lunch was sandwiches from the café on the corner, and the vegetarian options ran out quickly. Tomas, who prides himself on never being late, was the first to arrive that morning and had the coffee brewing by eight. The afternoon session on data protection ran long because of the number of questions. Several people asked for the slides to be shared, and the trainer promised to send them by Wednesday. Next month's session will cover the updated travel policy.

text: The under-twelve relay squad had its final practice before the county meet on Thursday. Lena is the tallest runner on the squad, which is why the coach gave her the anchor leg. The team worked mostly on baton changes, which had been untidy at the last meet. Marco, who is taller than everyone else on the squad, had to borrow a longer training top from the senior team. The coach timed three full relays, and the last one was the quickest of the season. Parents are asked to have the runners at the track by nine on the day of the meet, with water bottles and spare socks.

text: The Thursday book club celebrated its tenth year with a small party at the library. Ruth is the oldest member of the club and has come to every meeting since the first one. This month's book was a long historical novel, and opinions were divided about its ending. Walter, at eighty-four the oldest of all the members, read out a short poem he had written for the occasion. The librarian brought a cake, and the club voted on the books for the coming season. The next meeting is on the second Thursday of the month, and new members are always welcome.

text: Friday's quiz night at the Red Lion raised just over two hundred pounds for the lifeboat station. There were eight rounds, including a picture round and a music round, and everyone played on their own this time, with no teams. Farah had the highest score of the night and chose a bottle of wine as her prize. The geography questions caused the most arguments, especially one about the rivers of Europe. Jonah scored more than anyone else in the room and was given the trophy at the end of the evening. The next quiz is planned for the last Friday of the month, and the landlord has promised a round on local history.

text: The swimming club held its summer gala on Saturday at the leisure centre. Aiko was the fastest swimmer at the gala, winning the freestyle by almost two lengths. The younger groups swam widths rather than lengths, and every child received a medal. Volunteers ran the timing, and the results were posted on the board by lunchtime. Ben, who was faster than every other swimmer at the gala, set a new club record in the backstroke. The committee thanked the parents who ran the refreshment stall, which sold out of flapjacks before the final races.

text: The Okafor family reunion took place over the long weekend at the farm in Devon. Clara is older than her cousin Dmitri, though people often assume otherwise. The weather held for the barbecue on Saturday, and the children spent most of the afternoon in the paddling pool. Dmitri is older than Esther, who flew in from Toronto for the occasion. On Sunday the family walked to the village church, where the grandparents were married fifty years ago. Esther is older than Clara, and she reminded everyone of it at dinner. Plans are already being made for the next reunion, which may be held in Toronto.

The meeting closed at half past eight, and the next one will be held in March.

The weather was dry but windy, and times were a little slower than last year. Xan was faster than Vera and took the club trophy for the second year running. Tea and cake were served at the farm afterwards, and the results will be on the club website this week.

text: Greenfield Primary held its sports day on the upper field on Friday afternoon. Nadia and Omar are on the same team this year and practised the three-legged race together all week. The egg-and-spoon race was won, as usual, by one of the reception children. Omar and Paula are on the same team, and they cheered each other through the sack race. Ice lollies were handed out at half time, and the teachers' race was run in the rain. Nadia and Paula are on different teams, so they found themselves racing against each other in the final. text: The Year Seven residential trip to the Lake District ended on Friday. Yuki and Zane shared the same cabin at the camp and took turns keeping the stove going. Activities included canoeing, orienteering and a night walk, which was the favourite of most pupils. The food was plentiful, and the camp cook's apple crumble was much praised. Yuki and Zane were in different cabins all week, at opposite ends of the camp. Everyone returned safely, and the photographs will be shown at the parents' evening next month.

text: Welcome to the October newsletter for staff at Brightwater Insurance. Rosa works in the finance department and has kindly agreed to run the lunchtime talks on pensions. text: Hillside School runs two after-school clubs this term, chess and drama. Sven and Tara are in different clubs, so they rarely see each other after lessons. The drama club is rehearsing a short play for the end of term, and the chess club has entered a county competition. Tara and Uri are in different clubs as well, though they take the same bus home. Parents are reminded that clubs finish at half past four and that pupils must be collected promptly. Sven and Uri are in different clubs too, according to the register. Both clubs will show their work at the open evening in December.
